summary: This diff adds a generic, external-AI-facing reporting API gateway (GET /api/v1/reports/catalog, POST /api/v1/reports/definitions/{id}/run) plus a server-safe CSV/XLSX export builder with a standard OWASP-style CSV/formula-injection mitigation (leading =+-@ characters get a neutralizing single-quote prefix, verified recoverable in tests). I cross-checked the new routes against the two existing sibling routes (session-auth src/app/api/reports/definitions/[id]/run/route.ts and API-key-based src/app/api/v1/projexa/reports/definitions/[id]/run/route.ts) and confirmed the tenant-isolation pattern is identical and correct: orgId is always taken from the authenticated ctx (session or API key), never from the request body, and the new route's own tests include an explicit spoofing attempt plus a cross-org isolation test. The new requireReportsReadAccess() scope gate correctly implements OR-semantics (broad 'read' OR new narrow 'read:reports') and I traced api-key-auth.ts's scope parsing to confirm 'read:reports' flows through the comma-separated scopes column and the POST /api/settings/api-keys whitelist without being silently dropped, and that a key scoped only to 'read:reports' correctly cannot pass hasScope() checks on other /v1/* domains (proper narrowing). The db/schema.ts change is a comment-only edit (no real migration), and the terminology-guardrail-exemptions.yaml / ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml changes are routine governance bookkeeping. No .github/workflows/** files are touched. I was unable to execute bun test/tsc directly in this environment (bun is not installed here) so I relied on static tracing of call sites and signatures instead of re-running the worker's reported 2072/2072 test pass, but the code paths I traced are internally consistent and match established, already-merged conventions in this codebase.
